messages:
lena: heads-up — seeing gradual GPU memory growth on long-context chat loads (seq 4k) that looks like KV fragmentation + pagewalk churn on H100, not repro-ing the same way on A100. reduced reuse_hitrate and lots of small free holes.

sam: can you paste the minimal repro + perf counters?

lena: repro is simple: run the streaming benchmark with model x-13b-qlora, batch 8, seq 4096 for ~30m. command: `./run_stream.sh --model x-13b --batch 8 --seq 4096 --duration 1800`

lena: log excerpt:```
I kvcache: alloc_page id=0x2a size=64KB reuse_hits=3 evict_order=[pid:47, pid:89,...]
I kvcache: page_walk count=119843 walk_ms=2310 reuse_decay=0.003
W memory: hole_count=1272 max_hole=48KB total_free=3.2GB
I kvcache: eviction: evict_page id=0x2a refcount=1 -> freed=false
```

raj: that "evict_page ... refcount=1 -> freed=false" line stands out. sounds like a refcount/race on the coalescing path. if two threads try to merge adjacent free slots we may be leaving stale PT entries.

raj: hypothesis: page_insert has a fast-path that sets page->owner then does a relaxed store to PT. concurrent page_walk can see inconsistent header and skip decrementing reuse.

sam: do you have a diff?

raj: small patch HACK: change the relaxed store to an atomic cmpxchg that ensures owner is visible before we update the pt_index. i ran it locally w/ stress for 10k iterations and mem growth went flat. attaching pseudo:```
--- a/kvcache/page.c
+++ b/kvcache/page.c
@@
-    page->owner = owner; // relaxed store
-    pt[idx] = page->meta;
+    if (!atomic_cmpxchg(&page->owner, 0, owner)) {
+        // fallback serial path
+    }
+    smp_wmb(); // ensure owner visible before pt write
+    pt[idx] = page->meta;
```

marco: ran perf counters on both GPUs. results: H100 shows 2.1x L2 load miss + 4x atomic retries on the insert hot loop. A100 has lower atomic retry rate. attaching perf snippet:```
H100: cycles 1.2e9, l2_miss 4.3e6, atomic_retries 1.2e5
A100: cycles 9.8e8, l2_miss 2.1e6, atomic_retries 2.8e4
```

olivia: sounds like coalescing path causes cacheline ping-pong under H100 SM topology. we either need stronger per-page locking or a lock-free insertion that batches updates per-warp. lock would be simplest but may cost latency.

lena: agreed. current workaround (in canary) is to disable aggressive coalescing on H100 via runtime flag `--kvcache-coalesce=off`. that eliminates the leak but increases fragmentation overhead.

kv-bot: regression-test: kvcache-coalesce-off => PASS, kvcache-coalesce-on (master) => FAIL (memory_growth > 1.5GB after 30m).

sam: can we get a minimal failing unit test that reproduces it in CI? otherwise bisect on infra is noisy.

raj: I can write a stress unit that runs two threads doing insert+merge on adjacent pages with random timing, should reproduce within a few seconds under high contention. will PR tomorrow.

marco: also checked that the issue is worst when seq length distribution has high variance (mix of short prefixes + long tail). contiguous long KV writes force more merging across page boundaries. noted in perf traces.

olivia: ops question — do we enable the flag for canary clusters now or wait for patch?

lena: enabling on canary now. deploy-bot kicked: `canary/eng-runtime -> kvcache-coalesce=off` :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout started to canary pool (5 nodes), will monitor memory and latency for 30m.

sam: next steps: (1) raj PR with atomic/cmpxchg approach + unit test, (2) perf microbench to measure latency cost, (3) test on A100/H100/T4 and adjust per-arch heuristics, (4) re-enable coalescing with safety checks (fallback to serial if cmpxchg fails > N).

lena: adding note to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-7421 — label: kvcache, h100, regression, p0.

marco: FYI I saw a related kernel selector hiccup where a slower kernel increased contention (because it holds the insertion longer). will include kernel timing in the perf PR.

olivia: +1 on per-arch flagging. H100 likely needs conservative defaults until we get atomics correct.

sam: thanks all. if anyone on call can watch the canary alerts for the next 30m ping here. :eyes:
